newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Indonesia minister leaves Russia without arms deal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia minister leaves Russia without arms deal.

text.p: Indonesia's research and technology minister said on Wednesday he had signed no new defence contracts during a nine-day visit to Russia, but talks with Moscow would continue.
Jusuf Habibie, who is also also head of state-owned plane maker Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN), told a news conference he had met officials from Russia's aviation industry.
But asked if he had signed any contracts to buy either Sukhoi or MiG fighter jets, Habibie replied: "No, no."
He said any potential deals with Russia needed more consideration but talks on a range of economic issues would be continued by Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita in August.
"We will continue talks. Next month the chairman of the planning board, Professor Ginanjar, will come and have a follow-up meeting," he said.

Indonesian Air Force Chief-of-Staff Sutria Tubagus inspected Russian aircraft last month at the Paris Air Show after Indonesia expressed interest in buying Russian Sukhoi-30 and MiG-29 fighters, radars, guided missiles and helicopters.
Jakarta cancelled a plan to buy nine American F-16s in May in response to U.S. congressional criticism of Indonesia.
Habibie, who arrived in Russia on July 1, visited defence plants during his visit to Moscow and St Petersburg but gave no details of his discussions there.
